requirements.summary: The ledger must remain non-canonical execution memory and must not be cited as planning canon.
requirements.raw_excerpt: Ledger is execution memory only; it is not canonical and must not be cited in planning docs.

requirements.summary: Packet emission is prohibited until survivor-versus-retire contradictions are repaired in packet-planning inputs.
requirements.raw_excerpt: packet emission must not proceed until those target-level contradictions are repaired in packet-planning inputs

requirements.summary: Automation-first behavior is required with HITL disabled by default and critical/HITL issues surfaced to Dashboard, Orchestrator, and chat-thread resolution.
requirements.raw_excerpt: all tests/review paths are expected to be fully automated by default ... HITL is explicitly off by default ... issue must surface in: Dashboard, Orchestrator page, a spawned agent/thread in the chat window

requirements.summary: Policy transparency requires UI to explicitly show inherited, overridden, and effective values.
requirements.raw_excerpt: UI should explicitly show: `Inherited`, `Overridden`, `Effective` ... users should not need a separate modal just to understand resolution/inheritance/fallback

decisions.summary: The tab model stays split with distinct Progress, Seams, Node Graph, Evidence, History, and Ledger responsibilities instead of merging History and Ledger.
decisions.raw_excerpt: keep tabs separate: `Progress`, `Seams` ... `History` and `Ledger` should remain separate: `History` = chronological runtime story; `Ledger` = structured record inspection
decisions.decision_rationale: Separation preserves operational workflow clarity and avoids conflating timeline narrative with structured records.

decisions.summary: Hybrid governance is acceptable only when graph execution remains canonical and tiers are merely a derived human-facing lens.
decisions.raw_excerpt: hybrid is acceptable only if graph execution remains canonical and tiers become a derived human-facing lens
rejected_alternatives: Dual execution authority across tiers and graph

decisions.summary: Progress tab policy prefers a broad orchestrator widget catalog, with users able to disable or hide widgets.
decisions.raw_excerpt: Progress-tab widget direction is now firmer: err on the side of more orchestrator widget options rather than fewer; user can disable/hide widgets they do not want

data_shapes.summary: Concern records are first-class and must include identity, scope, severity, category, owner, lifecycle state, meaning, linkage, and visibility flags.
data_shapes.raw_excerpt: concern records should carry: identity, scope, severity, category, owner, lifecycle state, meaning/summary, linkage to evidence/artifacts/history/source records, visibility/attention flags

data_shapes.summary: Concern lifecycle states are enumerated as active, acknowledged, resolved, and dismissed.
Projection health states are modeled as current, refreshing, stale, and failed.
data_shapes.raw_excerpt: projection health states should conceptually include: `current`, `refreshing`, `stale`, `failed`

data_shapes.summary: Canonical persisted object inventory includes project, run, feature_seam, work_package, node, attempt, lane, snapshot, promotion, review, resolution_thread, and event.
data_shapes.raw_excerpt: canonical persisted objects should likely include at least `project`, `run`, `feature_seam`, `work_package`, `node`, `attempt`, `lane`, `snapshot`, `promotion`, `review`, `resolution_thread`, and `event`

data_shapes.summary: Child object schema direction defines required fields for attempt, lane, promotion, review, and resolution_thread records.
data_shapes.raw_excerpt: `attempt` should persist identity ... requested vs effective ... `lane` should persist ... worktree binding ... `promotion` ... `review` ... `resolution_thread` ...

data_shapes.summary: Parent object schema direction requires minimal field shapes for project, run, feature_seam, and work_package.

routing_rules.summary: Cross-tab deep-linking must carry selection, filter, and focus context rather than only switching tabs.
routing_rules.raw_excerpt: deep links should carry selection/filter/focus context, not merely switch tabs

routing_rules.summary: When projections degrade, execution-changing actions require fresh-enough state while observational and navigation actions can remain available with inline gating explanation.
routing_rules.raw_excerpt: actions that change execution/promotion/recovery/approval truth require fresh-enough projection state ... observational/navigation/export actions generally remain safe ... UI should explain gating inline

routing_rules.summary: Under stale projections, routing degrades to direct record-backed inspection with Ledger as trust anchor and action limited to current generation-matched records.
routing_rules.raw_excerpt: degrade from summary/projection surfaces to direct record-backed inspection ... `Ledger` and direct record views become the trust anchor ... only certain current/generation-matched direct records should support action

routing_rules.summary: Node Graph detail inspector evidence and artifact links must deep-link into Evidence with target selection/filter applied.
routing_rules.raw_excerpt: clicking evidence/artifact links in graph detail should deep-link into the Evidence tab with target selection/filter applied

routing_rules.summary: Settings scope hierarchy defines authoritative inheritance tiers from app/global through runtime-only computed truth.
routing_rules.raw_excerpt: Settings scope hierarchy direction now clarified: `App / Global` ... `Project` ... `Seam` ... `Package` ... `Node` ... `Actor / Role` ... `Runtime only` = computed truth, not user configuration

routing_rules.summary: Orchestrator chat-thread escalation patterns must not be back-projected onto normal conversational actor flows.
routing_rules.raw_excerpt: chat-thread resolution surfaces for blocked/HITL/critical Orchestrator events should not be projected backwards onto normal assistant/interviewer/requirements-builder conversation in the same way

verification_rules.summary: Before remediation or graph change, two additional subagents must validate an overseer-raised missing-work or correctness concern.
verification_rules.raw_excerpt: when an overseer finds missing work / wiring / design correctness issues, two additional subagents should be spawned to check whether the overseer's concern is valid before remediation or graph-change action proceeds

verification_rules.summary: Seam completion verification must fail when integration is weak, so package completion alone is insufficient.
verification_rules.raw_excerpt: if integration is weak, the feature seam is not complete; package completion is therefore necessary but not sufficient for seam completion

verification_rules.summary: Alert semantics must keep resolved, dismissed, and acknowledged distinct, and active blockers must not be dismissed or acknowledged in place of real resolution.
verification_rules.raw_excerpt: `resolved` = underlying condition actually changed ... `dismissed` = presentation hidden ... active blockers must not be dismissible ... blockers requiring real action must not be acknowledgeable in place of resolution

owner_consumer_obligations.summary: Orchestrator is obligated to consume canonical runtime scheduler contracts and event-driven runtime fields rather than owning schemas locally.
owner_consumer_obligations.raw_excerpt: `Plans/orchestrator-subagent-integration.md` treats Orchestrator as the primary consumer of canonical runtime scheduler contracts, not as a schema owner ... event-driven wakeups ... authoritative execution/update model

owner_consumer_obligations.summary: Usage and quota model ownership remains centered in usage docs, with storage and GUI docs as supporting consumers for runtime assumptions.
owner_consumer_obligations.raw_excerpt: `Plans/usage-feature.md` is the strongest current owner for usage/quota/alerts/analytics/product-shape discussion. `Plans/storage-plan.md` and `Plans/FinalGUISpec.md` also carry meaningful usage/runtime/event/GUI assumptions.

owner_consumer_obligations.summary: Ownership contract must keep blocked-owner labels, alert levels, and event families canonical while mapping operator visibility tiers by surface.
owner_consumer_obligations.raw_excerpt: blocked ownership should be normalized ... alert levels ... canonical event families should remain stable ... operator visibility should separate history-only, badge-worthy, attention-card-worthy, and chat-thread-worthy cases

owner_consumer_obligations.summary: Canonical concern records are created by runtime and overseer/corroboration/patch logic; workers may nominate findings but may not mint canonical concerns directly.
owner_consumer_obligations.raw_excerpt: canonical concerns should be created by runtime, package overseer, seam overseer, corroboration outcome, graph patch/state-transition logic ... workers may nominate findings but should not mint canonical concerns directly

owner_consumer_obligations.summary: Any provider-using actor must participate in shared pre-send and post-send account-health loop, including non-Orchestrator conversational actors.
owner_consumer_obligations.raw_excerpt: account selection / failover is not just an Orchestrator-node concern ... any provider-using actor must participate in the same pre-send and post-send account-health loop

stale_retirement_items.summary: Design language should retire ambiguous optional-JSON phrasing except for explicit manual inspection or export use.
stale_retirement_items.raw_excerpt: "optional JSON" wording should be removed from the design language unless JSON export is explicitly about manual inspection/export, not canonical storage

stale_retirement_items.summary: Legacy page-layer shadow event and schema ownership should be removed so Orchestrator remains a projection-and-controls consumer.
stale_retirement_items.raw_excerpt: remove shadow event/schema ownership from the page layer and tighten it around projections and controls only

open_questions.summary: The replacement name for the Tiers tab remains unresolved between Seams and equivalent variants.
open_questions.raw_excerpt: existing `Tiers` tab should be replaced by a seam/package-oriented tab (name still open; likely `Seams` or equivalent)

open_questions.summary: Concrete storage medium, owning paths, and worker handoff delivery mechanism for retry artifacts are still unresolved.
open_questions.raw_excerpt: "JSON-like" is too vague ... design still needs to pin down whether these artifacts are literally JSON/JSONL/redb-backed records/projections ... what concrete project-scoped paths ... how a worker actually receives the handoff packet ... remains an open design seam

open_questions.summary: Exact storage medium/path and worker handoff delivery mechanism remains unresolved and still open.
open_questions.raw_excerpt: exact storage medium/path/delivery mechanism remains an open design seam and needs to be specified concretely
open_questions.question_text: Which concrete storage medium/path and handoff delivery mechanism should own retry/handoff artifacts?

process_defects.summary: Packet planning currently contains survivor-versus-stale-retire token contradictions across four documented targets, blocking faithful packet emission.
process_defects.raw_excerpt: `packet_plan.json` currently contains at least four survivor/residue contradictions ... `TierContext`, `tier_id`, `github_api:github.com/<login>`, `approve_continue`

process_defects.summary: Current docs lack documented GUI surfaces for feature seams and work packages, indicating transfer-fidelity gap against newly agreed governance model.
process_defects.raw_excerpt: no documented GUI surface yet for `work package` ... no documented GUI surface yet for `feature seam` ... no documented seam-level acceptance / weak-integration / corroboration review affordance yet

process_defects.summary: Direct-record actionability must display trust markers (currentness, generation match, superseded, actionable), with saved views and sorting defaults defined per tab.
process_defects.raw_excerpt: direct record views that allow action should explicitly show currentness, generation match, superseded yes/no, actionable yes/no ... Orchestrator should support saved views ... History/Ledger default sort = newest first

process_defects.summary: Event classification and multi-project/account scoping constraints remain underdefined and require canonicalization to avoid runtime/UI drift.
process_defects.raw_excerpt: Next subtopic requested: classify which events are runtime-internal vs operator-visible vs chat-thread resolution events ... multi-project and multi-account identity/projection/storage implications

doc_hints.summary: Orchestrator and GUI specs should be updated to replace tier vocabulary with feature seam and work package governance objects.
doc_hints.raw_excerpt: `Plans/Orchestrator_Page.md` still defines tabs `Progress`, `Tiers`, `Node Graph Display`, `Evidence`, `History`, `Ledger` ... `Plans/FinalGUISpec.md` still references `phase/task/subtask` progress

doc_hints.summary: Storage and GUI canon should record that seglog/redb are canonical persistence layers while JSON/JSONL remain export or disposable projections.
doc_hints.raw_excerpt: `Plans/storage-plan.md` already declares: `seglog` = canonical append-only event source ... `redb` = durable KV ... JSONL mirror = disposable projector output ... `Plans/FinalGUISpec.md` aligns with this

doc_hints.summary: Usage documentation should capture multi-account extensions as an extension of existing usage projections rather than a second quota subsystem.
doc_hints.raw_excerpt: `Plans/usage-feature.md` is the strongest current owner ... new multi-account failover / account-threshold / effective-account behavior should extend the existing usage model and projections ... do not invent a second independent "account pressure" or "quota" subsystem

doc_hints.summary: Orchestrator integration contract should remain authoritative for canonical runtime-consumer boundaries.
doc_hints.raw_excerpt: `Plans/orchestrator-subagent-integration.md` treats Orchestrator as the primary consumer of canonical runtime scheduler contracts, not as a schema owner

doc_hints.summary: Run graph documentation should be aligned with seam/package governance and reduced tier-carryover assumptions.
doc_hints.raw_excerpt: `Plans/Run_Graph_View.md` describes the graph as live DAG execution, but node rendering still includes tier-type iconography and tier-oriented vocabulary

doc_hints.summary: Executor protocol references containing tier tokens should be reconciled with packet survivor/retire rules.
GitHub auth flow token-handling section appears in contradiction set and needs packet-plan reconciliation.
UI command catalog entries in contradiction set should be reconciled before packet emission.
